stops.note: Jean Nicot, the French ambassador in Lisbon, sent tobacco to Queen Catherine de' Medici in 1560 as a cure for headaches
Linnaeus named the tobacco genus after Nicot in his Species Plantarum of 1753
the chemical name followed; Wilhelm Posselt and Karl Reimann of Heidelberg isolated the pure alkaloid in 1828
borrowed from French; the US Surgeon General's 1988 report declared nicotine addictive

current_meaning: a toxic, addictive compound found in tobacco
